1.why: Text uses a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable line height and spacing between elements, though letter spacing is default rather than notably generous.

2.why: Instructions are in sentence case with no italics and no dense paragraphs; the only all-caps text is the small 'NORTHSTAR BANK' brand mark, not instructions.

3.why: Content sits in a narrow single-column card with large text and full-width buttons that would map cleanly onto a phone viewport.

4.why: Instructions are one or two short sentences in plain language, e.g. 'Enter the six-digit code sent to your phone.'

5.why: Only the phone field shows a placeholder example ('+447700900000'); the identity verification code input shows no example of the expected six-digit format.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is a two-line sentence, so the user is never required to read a long block of text to proceed.

7.why: The verification code had to be typed by hand ('123456') and no copy buttons or selectable secret text appear anywhere in the observed flow.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is offered on any observed step; manual key entry is the only method shown.

9.why: Fields are plain inputs with no visible autofill hints, no one-time-code support, and no password field, giving no evidence of password-manager support.

10.why: The 'Step X of 3' label, bold heading, and full-width coloured button identify the stage and primary action, though the black Logs bar visually competes with the button.

11.why: Each screen presents a single primary button (Continue / Verify and continue) with only a low-emphasis 'Use different details' alternative.

12.why: After continuing, the next screen plainly says a code was sent to your phone and what to enter, and after failure the banner says to try again, though the error wording is generic.

13.why: After the error the same form remains available with the entered code so the user can retry without visible penalty, but there are no reveal, hide, or re-request controls.

14.why: The banner 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' avoids blaming the user but does not state what the problem was (wrong or expired code) or how specifically to fix it.

15.why: No time limit is imposed on reading, and the stated 10-minute validity of the code is generous time to enter a six-digit code.
